snapshot: Chicago Nikkei 225 futures settled at 62,110, up 2,690 versus Osaka. Cash equities reopened from Golden Week above the 60,000 line.
The Nikkei opened at 60,241.31 and by 09:48 JST had pushed into the 62,000 area for the first time.
U.S. equities rallied on AMD's outlook and the AI semiconductor theme, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq setting new highs.
Crude fell sharply on U.S.-Iran agreement hopes, while USD/JPY moved back toward the low 156s, easing the worst of the 'bad yen' pressure.
The tape is broadly risk-on, but the most actionable checks are still stock-specific: AI leaders, earnings, shareholder returns and activist filings from the holiday gap.

drivers.driver: U.S. AI strength and lower crude drove a post-holiday risk-on open
drivers.why_today: AMD's strong outlook lifted AI semiconductor names, while lower oil improved sentiment. The Nikkei reclaimed the 60,000 line and AI-related heavyweights are pushing the index higher.

drivers.driver: USD/JPY has pulled back, easing import-cost concerns
drivers.why_today: Dollar/yen fell into the low 156s, reducing the intervention and bad-yen concerns that dominated near 160. That helps both domestic-demand and external-demand sentiment.

drivers.why_today: Oasis' stake in Plus Alpha, strong guidance from ARE and DMG Mori, and buybacks at DTS and Alinco provide clear stock-specific catalysts to verify after the open.

deep_dive.title: SoftBank Group: test whether the AI semiconductor rally can last beyond index-driven short covering

lines: The core catalyst is the AI semiconductor rally triggered by AMD's earnings and the read-through to Arm and AI infrastructure exposure.
Because SoftBank has major index impact, it is the most important single name for explaining the Nikkei's reclaiming of the 60,000 area.
During Japan's Golden Week break, AMD-led AI semiconductor strength drove U.S. equities higher, and SoftBank was up more than 11% by 09:48 JST in Tokyo.
The Nikkei moved into the 62,000 area for the first time, with AI and semiconductor heavyweights providing the main index lift.
Can the stock hold above the 6,000-yen area instead of fading after the opening short-covering burst.
Does the Arm and AI-semiconductor read-through remain visible through stock-specific turnover into the afternoon.
The AI semiconductor buyback wave fades and SoftBank gives back gains quickly.
Arm's volatile after-hours reaction or weaker U.S. tech futures hit sentiment toward the whole AI complex.
The stronger the index-driven flow, the more vulnerable the stock can become to profit-taking if the market turns.
The AI semiconductor catalyst is fresh, but the trade has a large positioning component, so price adjustments can be fast.
